title: How LLMs work for Web Devs: GPT in 600 lines of Vanilla JS - Ishan Anand
talk_summary: A workshop that reimplements GPT-2 small in ~600 lines of vanilla JavaScript so web developers can step through tokenization, embeddings, attention, MLP, and sampling in the browser debugger. It is an educational explainer of transformer internals, not a talk about operating agent systems, and its only operational advice is a short Q&A aside on empirical prompt evaluation.

takeaways.technique: Treat prompting as empirical; benchmark before trusting prompt folklore
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite the Prompting Report and Ethan Mollick's replication, which tested politeness/'grandma' style prompt tricks across models and found they stopped helping on later models; conclusion is to benchmark prompts with evals rather than assume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to treat it scientifically. You you can have theories about how the model works, but you don't really know till you test it.

takeaways.technique: Keep prompts clean because fixed compute is spent on noise
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the forward pass is a fixed formula, so tokens spent on typos or irrelevant material consume capacity that would otherwise go to the actual task; for reasoning models this matters less because they can iterate internally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you make the prompt do more work, if the prompt is going to make the model do more work, you kind of think of it like it loses some ability to do some other thinking.
